post.description: Creates a user account, signs the user in and sends a verification email (with MAIL_MAILER=log the email, including the verification link, is written to storage/logs/laravel.log). The tokens are NOT in the JSON body: the response sets two HttpOnly cookies, `access_token` (path /, lifetime JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes, default 15) and `refresh_token` (path /api/auth, lifetime JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days, default 30). In Swagger UI the browser stores them, so later calls such as GET /api/auth/me work automatically in the same browser. Account and first session are created in one transaction; a sign-up that loses a race for the same email gets the same 422 as the validation rule. Rate limited (limiter `auth-register`): 10 requests per minute per IP and 3 per minute per email from the same IP (no bucket is keyed by the email alone, so nobody can block an address from other IPs).

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description: Checks the credentials and signs the user in. The tokens are NOT in the JSON body: the response sets the HttpOnly cookies `access_token` (path /) and `refresh_token` (path /api/auth). The browser keeps them, so later calls (GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/refresh, POST /api/auth/logout) work automatically in the same browser. A wrong password, an unknown email, an account without a password (a social sign-up that never set one) and a disabled account all return the same 401 and take as long (the last two are checked against a dummy hash). Optional `remember` (default true) chooses persistent or session cookies (see LoginRequest). Rate limited: every request counts in a per-IP bucket (limiter `auth-login`, 20 per minute), and failed sign-ins count per email and IP (5 per minute; a successful sign-in clears it), so failures from other IPs never lock the owner out. Both answer the same 429 (message `Too Many Attempts.`, with `Retry-After`).

200.description: Signed in. Tokens are set as HttpOnly cookies (both are session cookies when `remember` is false; see LoginRequest).

Set-Cookie.description: Two HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies (Secure outside local/testing): `access_token=<JWT>; Path=/; Max-Age=JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes (default 15)` and `refresh_token=<opaque token>; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=until the refresh token expires: JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days (default 30), but never later than JWT_REFRESH_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS days (default 90) after the original login`.

401.description: Invalid credentials (unknown email, wrong password or disabled account).

post.summary: Rotate the tokens using the refresh cookie
post.description: No request body. Reads the HttpOnly `refresh_token` cookie (sent automatically by the browser after login or register, because its path is /api/auth), revokes it and issues a new `access_token` and `refresh_token` pair as cookies. If the cookie is missing, invalid, expired or already used, returns 401 and clears both cookies, and an already-used, expired or disabled-account token also revokes every token of that login. Exception: a token rotated less than JWT_REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS (default 20) ago whose replacement is still valid (two tabs refreshing at once, or a retry after a lost response) gets a new token pair of the same login instead. A login can be refreshed for at most JWT_REFRESH_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS days (default 90); after that this returns 401 and the user must sign in again. Rate limited (limiter `auth-refresh`): 30 requests per minute per IP.

parameters.name: refresh_token
parameters.description: HttpOnly refresh token cookie set by login/register/refresh. Sent automatically by the browser.

200.description: New token pair issued as HttpOnly cookies.

Set-Cookie.description: Two HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies (Secure outside local/testing): `access_token=<JWT>; Path=/; Max-Age=JWT_ACCESS_TTL minutes (default 15)` and `refresh_token=<opaque token>; Path=/api/auth; Max-Age=until the refresh token expires: JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS days (default 30), but never later than JWT_REFRESH_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS days (default 90) after the original login`.

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked refresh token. Both auth cookies are cleared.

schema.example: access_token=deleted; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; path=/; httponly

get.description: Returns the current user. Authenticate with the `access_token` cookie (set automatically by login/register in the same browser) or with an `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` header. The bearer header wins when both are present. The access token is short-lived (default 15 minutes): call POST /api/auth/refresh when it expires. Returns 401 when the token is missing, invalid or expired, or the user no longer exists or is disabled.

get.summary: Open the verification link (signed link; changes nothing)
get.description: The signed link from the verification email (valid 60 minutes). Changes nothing and needs no session, so a mail scanner or link preview that prefetches it verifies nothing: a correctly signed link redirects (302) to the public confirmation page FRONTEND_URL/account-link/verify-email?id={id}&hash={hash}&expires={expires}&signature={signature} (the link's own values), whose click POSTs the same signed URL. A missing or tampered signature redirects to FRONTEND_URL/account-link/result?kind=verify-email&outcome=invalid, a correctly signed expired one with `outcome=expired`. Rate limited (limiter `auth-verify-email`) to 20 requests per minute per IP, shared with the POST.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: SHA-1 hash of the user's email address.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Unix timestamp at which the signed link expires (part of the signed URL).

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: URL signature generated by the server (part of the signed URL).

302.description: Redirect to FRONTEND_URL/account-link/verify-email with the signed link's id, hash, expires and signature; on a bad signature to FRONTEND_URL/account-link/result?kind=verify-email&outcome=invalid|expired.

post.description: The click on the public confirmation page: same path and query string as the mailed link (the signature covers it); no login is required. Marks `email_verified_at` and answers `{"outcome": "success"}`. Idempotent: when the address is already verified (a second click, or two at once) nothing changes and the answer is `already-verified`. `invalid` when the account no longer exists or its address changed since the link was mailed. Rate limited (limiter `auth-verify-email`) to 20 requests per minute per IP, shared with the GET.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: SHA-1 hash of the user's email address.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Unix timestamp at which the signed link expires (part of the signed URL).

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: URL signature generated by the server (part of the signed URL).

post.description: Sends a new verification email if the account exists and is not verified yet. Always returns the same generic 200 message so it does not reveal whether the email is registered. With MAIL_MAILER=log the email (and its signed link) is written to storage/logs/laravel.log. Rate limited (limiter `auth-resend-verification`): 10 requests per minute per IP and 3 per minute per email from the same IP.

200.description: Generic response (same whether or not the account exists).

example.message: If the account exists and is unverified, a verification email has been sent.
The email field must be a valid email address.

email: The email field must be a valid email address.

post.description: Sends a password reset email (link valid 60 minutes) if the email is registered. Always returns the same generic 200 message so it does not reveal whether the email exists. The email contains the reset `token` needed by POST /api/auth/reset-password; with MAIL_MAILER=log it is written to storage/logs/laravel.log. The email is sent after the response, tried twice (1 s apart). Rate limited (limiter `auth-forgot-password`): 10 requests per minute per IP and 3 per minute per email from the same IP.

200.description: Generic response (same whether or not the email is registered).

example.message: If that email is registered, a password reset link has been sent.

post.summary: Reset the password with a reset token
post.description: Sets a new password using the `token` from the password reset email (see POST /api/auth/forgot-password; with MAIL_MAILER=log the email is in storage/logs/laravel.log). Does not sign the user in. An account without a password (social sign-up) gets its first one this way, and since the emailed token proves the inbox, that password counts as proof for email changes and account deletion. Returns 422 with a plain message when the token is invalid or expired, and 422 with field errors when validation fails. A token works once (two requests with the same token: only the first succeeds). A successful reset also marks an unverified address verified (the emailed token proves the inbox), signs every device out, and mails a `Your WatchWise password was changed` notice. Rate limited (limiter `auth-reset-password`): 10 requests per minute per IP and 5 per minute per email from the same IP.

422.description: Invalid or expired reset token ({"message": "Invalid or expired reset token."}), or validation failed (ValidationError with `errors`).

value.message: The password field confirmation does not match.

password: The password field confirmation does not match.

get.summary: Start a social login (redirect to the provider)
get.description: Redirects (302) the browser to the Google, GitHub or Discord consent screen and sets a short-lived HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax state cookie (10 minutes) whose value `<provider>:<random>` is checked at that provider's callback. The cookie is named `__Host-oauth_state` (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) outside local/testing and `oauth_state` there. Requires the provider's OAuth client id, secret and redirect URI (`*_CLIENT_ID`, `*_CLIENT_SECRET`, `*_REDIRECT_URI`) in .env; when any is missing or still `CHANGE_ME` it redirects (302) to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=error&reason=provider_unavailable instead, without setting the cookie. Swagger UI cannot follow this cross-site redirect usefully: open the URL directly in the browser address bar instead. Rate limited (limiter `auth-social-redirect`): 30 requests per minute per IP; over the limit it redirects (302) to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=error&reason=too_many_attempts (with Retry-After) instead of answering 429. Any other provider returns 404.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's OAuth authorization page, or to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=error&reason=provider_unavailable when the provider is not configured.

Location.description: Provider authorization URL (accounts.google.com, github.com or discord.com), or the frontend failure page.

Set-Cookie.description: __Host-oauth_state=<provider>:<random>; Max-Age=600; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (named oauth_state, without Secure, in local/testing)

get.summary: Social login callback (called by the provider)
get.description: The provider redirects the browser here after consent; it is not meant to be called by hand (it needs the provider's `code` and the `state` matching the state cookie, and configured OAuth keys). On success it signs the user in (an identity already linked signs in to its account even without an email; otherwise the account is linked by verified email or created), sets the HttpOnly `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies and redirects (302) to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=success. On failure it redirects to FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback?status=error&reason=<reason>, where reason is one of: invalid_state (state missing, not matching the cookie, or issued for another provider), provider_unavailable (the provider's client id, secret or redirect URI is not configured), access_denied (the user cancelled the consent screen), too_many_attempts (the rate limit below), provider_error (the provider exchange failed or returned no user id, an OAuth error other than access_denied, or any unexpected error; reported to the logs), email_required (the identity is not linked yet and the provider returned no email, e.g. a GitHub account without a verified primary email, since Socialite reads /user/emails and keeps only the verified primary address, or a Discord account without an email), email_unverified (Google or Discord has not verified the email), account_disabled (nothing about the account is changed). The state cookie is cleared on every outcome, so a state works once. The cookie is named `__Host-oauth_state` (Secure, Path=/, no Domain) outside local/testing and `oauth_state` there. Rate limited (limiter `auth-social-callback`): 30 requests per minute per IP; over the limit it redirects with reason too_many_attempts instead of answering 429. Any other provider returns 404.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: OAuth state echoed by the provider; must equal the state cookie and start with `<provider>:`.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: OAuth error sent by the provider instead of a code; `access_denied` when the user cancelled.

parameters.name: oauth_state
parameters.description: HttpOnly state cookie set by GET /api/auth/social/{provider}. Named `__Host-oauth_state` outside local/testing.

302.description: Redirect to the frontend with `status` (success|error) and, on error, `reason` (invalid_state|provider_unavailable|access_denied|too_many_attempts|provider_error|email_required|email_unverified|account_disabled) query params. On success the auth cookies are set.

Set-Cookie.description: The state cookie cleared on every outcome; on success also the access_token and refresh_token HttpOnly cookies (see POST /api/auth/login).

AuthResponse.description: Body of register/login/refresh. The tokens are NOT here: they are set as HttpOnly cookies `access_token` and `refresh_token`.

expires_at.description: When the access token (access_token cookie) expires, ISO 8601.

name.description: Trimmed; 1 to 255 characters. May not contain control characters (Cc: line breaks, tabs, NUL), the line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029), bidirectional embeddings, overrides and isolates (U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069), direction marks (U+200E, U+200F, U+061C), the BOM (U+FEFF) and unassigned, surrogate or private-use code points; the joiners U+200D/U+200C and variation selectors stay allowed, so emoji sequences work: 422 `The name may not contain line breaks, tabs or invisible direction characters.`

email.description: Trimmed and stored lowercase. Must be unique in any letter case (`Jane@Example.com` is taken when `jane@example.com` exists).

password.description: The shared new-password rule: at least 8 characters with at least one letter and one number, at most 72 bytes in UTF-8 (bcrypt reads no further; accented, non-Latin and emoji characters count as 2 to 4 bytes), no NUL byte.
At most 1024 bytes (far above the 72 bytes bcrypt reads, so passwords chosen before new ones were capped still work); no NUL byte.

remember.description: "Remember me". Optional, default true (the behaviour before the option existed). true: cookies that expire with their tokens, a refresh token sliding JWT_REFRESH_TTL_DAYS (30) days, the login ending JWT_REFRESH_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS (90) days after sign-in. false: both cookies are session cookies (no Expires/Max-Age, gone when the browser closes), the refresh token slides JWT_REFRESH_SESSION_HOURS (24) hours, the login ends JWT_REFRESH_SESSION_FAMILY_MAX_DAYS (7) days after sign-in. Kept by every refresh and by the session a password set or change re-issues.

token.description: Reset token from the password reset email.

password.description: The shared new-password rule (same as registration): at least 8 characters with at least one letter and one number, at most 72 bytes in UTF-8, no NUL byte.
